newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TAIWAN SELLS THREE SEPT DIESEL CARGOES IN TENDER.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN SELLS THREE SEPT DIESEL CARGOES IN TENDER.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) awarded three cargoes in its 0.3-percent sulphur diesel sell tender for September lifting, a company source said.
The three cargoes, loading on separate dates between September 5-30, were awarded at discounts of between 20 cents to 40 cents per barrel under Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
The bigger discounts were for cargoes loading earlier in September, reflecting the contango market condiction.
Traders said all three cargoes were awarded to a Singapore trader, but this could not be confirmed with CPC.

In its last tender, CPC awarded two August cargoes to a Swiss trader and a US major at $20.30-$20.50 per barrel. Prior to this, it sold a July 23-27 lifting cargo at around a 50 cents discount to spot Singapore prices fob.
